title: Naturality and independence of the smooth purity map
statement:
In the situation of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity],
the smooth purity map $\gamma_{f,K}$ of
[def-pur-smooth-purity-map] is natural in $K$, and it is
independent of the choices made in its construction.

proof.text: For each intrinsic finite-Tor constructible input K, lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin supplies a bounded constructible etale representative. Use the canonical derived realization equivalence and the counit to obtain e : nu* J ≅ E.inverse K. Convert the boundedness interval and constructible homology to the source boundedConstructible predicate. Transport the intrinsic Tor interval across E.counitIso and apply lem-exc-intrinsic-tor-amplitude-transport to identify its Tor predicate with the fixed-coefficient tensor predicate. The comparison Hom bijection lifts e.hom followed by E.inverse.map u followed by e′.inv to an etale arrow a. Apply lem-pur-tensor-map-naturality to a and its compatibility equation to obtain naturality of theta.

Precompose the theta square with tensor of the fixed inverse diagonal orientation. Naturality of the tensor bifunctor moves this inverse orientation across the map in the first factor. The characterization existsUnique_smoothPurityTensorMap in def-pur-smooth-purity-map identifies both presentation composites with the chosen intrinsic tensor map. Applying the realization functor and its composition law gives naturality of smoothPurityTensorMap.

The HEq clause of existsUnique_smoothPurityTensorShift in def-pur-smooth-purity-map identifies the published tensor shift with smoothPurityTensorShiftGeneric. For the latter, apply NatTrans.shift_app_comm to the first-factor tensor transformation, cancel the commShiftIso component, and compose with the shiftFunctorCompIsoId cancellation. Naturality of that first-factor tensor transformation at the cancellation arrow completes the square. Specialize to r=2d, and paste with the previous tensor-map square. Functor.map_comp and associativity give exactly the first conjunct.

For two etale presentations of K, the specification of the same chosen map in existsUnique_smoothPurityTensorMap identifies it with each smoothPurityTensorMapInPresentation. Reverse the first equality and compose with the second. This proves the second conjunct, without selecting any additional orientation, resolution, compactification, or arbitrary witness of mere existence.

In the situation of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity],
the smooth purity map $\gamma_{f,K}$ of
[def-pur-smooth-purity-map] is natural in $K$, and it is

proof.text:
Naturality in $K$ is the naturality of the tensor formula
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], of the twist
isomorphisms [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and of the
identification of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] (in the
object and in the morphism, all steps of the construction of
[def-pur-smooth-purity-map] being canonical derived
transformations).
The independence of the choices: the construction contains no
choices at all – the identification of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] is the unique one normalized
on the standard pairs and compatible with base change and etale
localization ([thm-pur-dnc-invariance]), the tensor formula and
the twist isomorphisms are canonical, and the normalization on the
standard pairs is the single one of vector-bundle integration
([cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]), fixed by the projective-line trace
$t_q(c_1(\mathcal O(1)))=1$. Equivalently it is fixed by the Kummer
boundary of the coordinate ([thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] and
[thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]): in relative dimension $d$ the
product of the Kummer boundaries of the coordinates integrates to the
fixed sign $(-1)^d$ ([cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity]), so
neither normalization involves a choice.
